deepdive.sec: Private-Sector Bank (old-private, Tamil Nadu — MSME + gold-loan led, 122-year-old franchise)

bull_bear.body:
- **CRAR not quantified** — only *"we are one of the banks with a very decent capital adequacy ratio."*
- **ECL transition is the live capital call:** requirement ~**0.45% of the loan book**, capital consumption
  *"should not be more than 0.65% on the CAR"*, and the year's asset-quality improvement already saved
  Rs. 150-180 cr of provision / ~0.90% of capital versus a year-ago simulation. Incremental flow impact
  *"very, very negligible"* because the book is *"completely a secured player."*
- **Deposit growth deliberately paced to credit growth** to hold CD ratio at 85% — *"our deposit growth is
  aligning with our credit growth which is helping us to maintain the desired CD ratio."* LCR 150%.
- No buyback, dividend, fund-raise or inorganic action was discussed on this call.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Guided margin + cost double step-down in Q2:** NIM 3.78% → 3.65-3.70% and C/I 45.42% → 47-48% land in the
  same quarter, both management-flagged. ROA guidance (1.55-1.65%) says it is absorbed — that is the thing to
  verify, not the individual lines.
- **Fee income shortfall:** other income Rs. 243 cr vs a Rs. 259-300 cr run-rate; the ROA bridge to 1.65% exit
  explicitly *requires* other income at 300-320. MD's answer was a hope, not a plan: *"hopefully we will catch
  it up, Q2-Q3-Q4."*
- **MSME growth gap vs system:** analysts pressed twice that system MSME is growing >20% while CUB is ~15%.
  Explained by Rs. 900 cr/month repayment + utilisation 73% → 70% + pricing caution. If utilisation does not
  recover on the India-EU/textile pickup, the "2-3% above industry" guidance is at risk.
- **Gold concentration at ~31% of a Rs. 67,645 cr book with 62.07% average LTV.** MD gave the gold-price
  stress ladder himself: *"at a 5% drop, we will be at 65% LTV. At a 10% drop, we will be at 69% LTV. At a 15%
  drop, we will be at 73% LTV. And at a 20% drop, we will be at 78% LTV."* He is comfortable; a sharp gold
  correction is nonetheless the single largest quantified sensitivity disclosed on the call.
- **Deposit repricing:** *"term deposit rates on the verge of rising due to high demand"* — a system-level
  funding-cost risk, not CUB-specific.
- **Yield-driven attrition in large industry:** the book already round-tripped Rs. 22,500 Mn → Rs. 15,000 Mn →
  Rs. 19,000 Mn on price discipline.
- **Leadership transition:** first call under a new MD & CEO. Continuity is asserted (predecessor Dr. N.
  Kamakodi still heads the CSR Foundation) but whether he joins as Non-Executive Director was left **openly
  unanswered**: *"With respect to Non-Executive Director, I think we should ask only him. I haven't asked till
  now."*
- **West Asia crisis:** management sees **no** transmission — *"domestic consumption remained largely insulated
  from the impact of West Asia crisis"*, no SMA spike. Watch-item only because it is an external variable, not
  because CUB reported stress.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body:
Confident, specific and unusually willing to give ratios on demand (SMA 0/1/2 split, LTV stress ladder,
segment-wise pricing, borrowing cost in rupees) — the CFO/ED never had to step in. The distinguishing trait is
**pricing discipline stated as principle rather than tactic**: refusing to raise gold rates on agri borrowers
*"who want to harvest"*, letting large-industry accounts exit rather than cut rate, capping DSA sourcing at
1-2%, refusing tickets above Rs. 10 cr, and reframing an utilisation decline as borrower prudence. Guidance is
set *below* the delivered quarter on NIM, C/I and ROA, and the MD said so explicitly: *"we wanted to be a
realistic in the numbers what we commit."* Two soft spots: the fee-income answer was *"hopefully we will catch
it up"* with no mechanism, and the Kamakodi board question was deflected. Tone on the franchise is
custodial — *"it's truly a great honour and privilege to lead the 122-year-old franchisee."*
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The reported 45.42% cost-to-income is structurally the low point of FY27, by design** — branch roll-out was
  front-loaded into Q1 and the staff hike starts in July. The "beat" on C/I and the guide to 47-48% are the
  same fact seen twice, not a deterioration.
- **The ROA bridge runs through fee income, not through lending.** 1.57% → 1.65% exit is explicitly built on
  other income going Rs. 243 cr → Rs. 300-320 cr; NIM and C/I are both guided *worse*. So the ROA guidance is a
  bet on processing fee + suit recovery + insurance — and insurance is the one they admit *"we really don't
  push that much."*
- **Utilisation, not demand, is the growth swing factor.** 73% → 70% is worth ~2-3% of MSME growth on
  management's own arithmetic — bigger than any pricing or competition effect discussed on the call, and it is
  a variable CUB does not control.
- **Gold growth is a distribution artefact as much as a gold-price artefact:** *"it is a function of 700 to
  1,000 branches what you are seeing now in uptick."* That reframes the gold-share question from risk appetite
  to branch maturity.
- **The ECL saving is a hidden dividend of the 12-quarter asset-quality grind** — Rs. 150-180 cr of provision
  and ~0.90% of capital that the bank does *not* have to find, purely because SMA went 7.12% → 2.85%.
- **The MF-into-other-income reclassification** (Rs. 700 cr → Rs. 12 cr) understates investment yield by 25 bps
  and flatters other income — worth normalising before comparing CUB's other-income trajectory to peers.
- Management sees the **India-EU agreement as an MSME credit-demand event**, not a corporate one — Tirupur
  knitwear first. That is a read-through most bank calls did not make.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Capital position at June'2026: Tier-I Capital 101,161 mn (deck's June'2026 column shows Tier-I CRAR 20.97% and Total CRAR 21.73%), against total risk weight of 507,968 mn; the performance overview states CRAR 21.73% (Basel III) of which core CRAR 20.97%.
- Capital is overwhelmingly Tier-I: Tier-II capital of only 3,869 mn at June'2026 versus 5,346 mn at Mar'2026, and Tier-II has been shrinking while Tier-I builds.
- Reserves and Surplus of 109,179 mn at Q1 FY 2027 against Share Capital of 991 mn; deposits 793,423 mn and borrowings 51,703 mn support a total balance sheet of 983,886 mn.
- The deck's stated return anchors are ROA of 1.57% described as "our long term average" and ROE of 14.37%.
- Restructuring exposure has been steadily worked down: restructured standard advances are 0.66% of gross advances at Jun-26 (₹4,464 mn across 566 borrowers) versus 5.91% at Sep-21 (₹22,478 mn across 1,976 borrowers).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Gold loans:** ~30-31% of advances, targeted 31-32%, ceiling 33%. Pricing: **agri 10-10.50%**, **non-agri
  11-11.50%** — agri deliberately **100 bps cheaper** (*"Genuinely, we are there for agri. So, we lend it at
  least 100 bps lesser"*). Blended gold yield ~10.6%, raised only **20-25 bps over the last one year**.
  **Branch-led product**: branch count 700 → 800 → **1,000**, which MD says is the real driver of non-agri gold
  growth. Average **LTV 62.07%**; agri LTV runs 5-7% higher than non-agri.
- **MSME vs "business enterprises":** *"Business enterprises is a non-MSME"* — an exposure with **no Udyam
  registration** (Rs. 18,827 Mn as disclosed). *"Large industries and services are predominantly MSME only."*
- **Large industry:** defined as borrower turnover **Rs. 750 cr and above**. Book was **Rs. 22,500 Mn at
  31-Dec-2025 → Rs. 15,000 Mn → Rs. 19,000 Mn** now; the fall was customers exiting on price plus utilisation
  (see §13). Explicitly *not* ECLGS-related funding.
- **Retail secured / LAP:** priced 9.60-9.70%; MSME 9.30-9.40%. *"retail is also picking up nicely for us in
  secured lending."*
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **Primary-banker relationship as an underwriting edge** — the reason MD dismisses competition as an
  explanation for the utilisation drop: *"competition cannot be a function for utilization, that too when you
  are a primary banker for majority of your book… If you are a primary banker and if you are monitoring where
  the money is going and where the money is coming from… more or less, the 'Kundali' is there with you."*
- **Branch-captive gold franchise, not a sourcing franchise:** *"we are predominantly branch-driven customer
  base and we get the customers who walk into the branch and pledges"* — hence *"we don't see much threat to
  gold loans from the competition at these junctures"*, and DSA sourcing is capped at 1-2% of the book.
- **Structural low-cost deposit position:** *"traditionally, you would be aware that we are not the highest
  payers in deposits"* — evidenced by cost of deposits falling to 5.56% in a quarter when peers were paying up.
- **Asset quality as a capital moat, quantified:** because SMA fell 7.12% → 2.85% over a year, the ECL
  requirement is 0.45% instead of what would have been 0.60-0.65% — *"if we would have simulated this ECL a
  year back, our requirement would have been another Rs. 150 crores-Rs. 180 crores more… and our capital would
  have dropped by 0.90% or so."*
business.title: 6a. Moat & competitive position

business.body:
| Challenge (their words) | Beneficiary stock(s) — NSE · BSE · Sector | Loser | Why / conviction |
|---|---|---|---|
| Large-industry borrowers repricing away: *"the rates were not conducive, they wanted to exit, we said fine. So, those customers exited us because of the yield pressure. We do not want to reduce the rate"* | Finer-priced large lenders that absorb the ceded corporate volume — **HDFCBANK · 500180** ✅, **ICICIBANK · 532174** ✅, **PNB · 532461** ✅ (all Private/Public-Sector Bank) | CUB — large-industry book Rs. 22,500 Mn (31-Dec-2025) → Rs. 15,000 Mn → Rs. 19,000 Mn | CUB is explicitly conceding volume rather than price at the ≥Rs. 750 cr-turnover end; the volume goes to whoever will price it. Named as a class by CUB, not as specific banks. **Med** |
| Term-deposit repricing: *"term deposit rates on the verge of rising due to high demand… we expect the cost of deposits may slightly increase in the next few quarters, which will impact NIM levels by around 5 bps"* | Deposit-franchise-rich universal banks least forced to pay up — **HDFCBANK · 500180** ✅, **ICICIBANK · 532174** ✅ | CUB (cost of deposits 5.56% → guided 5.60-5.70%) and other deposit-price-taker mid-caps — **KARURVYSYA · 590003** ✅, **MAHABANK · 532525** ✅ | A system-wide funding-cost event; relative winners are those with structurally cheaper liabilities. CUB partly insulated (*"we are not the highest payers in deposits"*). **Med** |
| MSME working-capital demand softness: utilisation *"used to be 73% on an average, this has come down to 70%"*, against *"Rs. 900 crores of repayment per month"* | _unmapped_ — no listed name in `companies.csv` / `products.csv` resolves as a beneficiary of borrower under-utilisation | MSME-concentrated lenders' loan growth — CUB, and **KARURVYSYA · 590003** ✅ (RAM/MSME-led old-private peer) | Cost CUB ~2-3% of MSME growth on management's own arithmetic. No beneficiary forced; leaving unmapped per SPEC §4. **Med (as a headwind), beneficiary Low** |
| Gold-loan competition: *"as everyone is expanding in taking market share of the gold loan"* — and CUB refuses to re-price up (*"It's not possible… we don't want to burden them"*) | Specialist gold-loan NBFCs with independent distribution ⭐ — **no listed name resolves within `companies.csv` / `products.csv`; left unmapped rather than sourced externally** | Not CUB by its own account (*"we don't see much threat… at these junctures"*; self-capped at 31-33%) | CUB forgoes pricing power it says it has, in agri specifically. Beneficiary set is real but outside our curated universe — SPEC §4 forbids resolving it on the web. **Conviction on the beneficiary: unresolved** |

> **Positive read-throughs named by management (not challenges, recorded so they are not lost):** India-EU trade
> agreement → **Tirupur textiles** (*"people are really gung-ho… particularly in the textile space"*);
> **Sriperumbudur auto/automobile** cluster; **paper & corrugated boxes in Kangeyam / Palladam** — nearest name
> in our universe **JKPAPER · 532162** ✅ (Integrated Paper & Packaging), though CUB spoke about local
> MSME converters, not JK Paper. Do not over-map.

---
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- SME/MSME focus is the core identity: the bank funds SMEs and MSMEs on a need-based, granular, "fully collateralized" lending strategy, with ~37% of the loan book in this segment, framed as helping build a resilient India in line with Viksit Bharat 2047.
- 120+ years of dedicated service as a Swadeshi Bank, having withstood World Wars, the Great Depression, the sub-prime crisis and the pandemic, with "continuous & consistent profitability all throughout 120+ years" - described as one of the few banks in the world to sustain more than 100 years with continuous profitability.
- Pan-India presence built outward from an original focus on farmers and traders of the Cauvery delta region, now spread from Kanyakumari to Jammu with 1000+ branches, aiming to augment the business potential of semi-urban, urban and unbanked rural areas.
- Diversified, low-concentration asset profile: advances to the top 20 group borrowers contribute 6.68% and the top 20 individual borrowers around 6.42%, with lower ticket-size lending backed by adequate collaterals and prudent sectoral and borrower exposure limits.
- Management continuity is presented as a governance asset - only 8 CEOs appointed in 122 years, with a strong board where the majority of directors are independent.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Capital] Share Capital rises from 743 mn (FY 2026) and 741 mn (Q1 FY 2026) to 991 mn at Q1 FY 2027 in the balance sheet, a material change in equity capital that the deck presents without any accompanying explanation of the issuance.
- [Credit ratings] Ratings as listed in the deck: CRISIL A1+ for Certificate of Deposits; CARE Edge AA- Issuer Rating; ICRA AA Issuer Rating and A1+ for Certificate of Deposits.
- [Shareholding] Well diversified investor base at 30 June 2026: MF, IFI and Banks 34.50%, Public 32.17%, FPI 18.65%, QIB 9.14%, NRI 2.42%, Corp Bodies 2.02%, Others 1.10%; largest institutional holders are HDFC AMC 9.32%, SBI AMC 8.26%, Axis Mutual Fund 4.93% and HSBC Mutual Fund 3.65% (subsidiaries/associates consolidated).
- [Leadership] R. Vijay Anandh is MD & CEO with over 28 years of banking experience, previously Group EVP & Business Head - Retail Assets & Collections and Group EVP & Chief Credit Officer for retail businesses at RBL Bank - a retail-assets background at the head of a historically MSME-centric bank.
- [Awards] Q1 awards: PFRDA Atal Pension Yojana (APY) Excellence; "Innovative Bank of the Year" at the India Banking Summit & Awards 2026; "Best AI Adoption - BFSI" at the AI Summit and Award 2026.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- NIM 3.78% held with **yield on advances flat at 9.79%** and **cost of deposits down to 5.56%**; the entire
  cost-of-funds increase came from **borrowings/refinance (Rs. 72.50 cr → Rs. 94 cr)**, not deposits.
- The guided **5 bps NIM hit** is sourced to term-deposit repricing, not asset yields. Asset-side yields are
  described as defended-by-refusal: gold pricing unchanged, large-industry accounts allowed to exit rather than
  match, *"we are also slightly cautious on pricing now."*
- **Gold-loan pricing is deliberately inelastic upward.** Asked why not raise 100 bps and let growth fall:
  *"It's not possible… Genuinely, we are there in the agricultural space. So, really, we don't want to burden
  them… We really don't want to go overboard."* Only *"0.1%, 0.2%, if necessary, and if all the other players
  increase it."*
- **Cost side steps up in Q2:** branch openings front-loaded (already done), **staff hike effective from July**
  → C/I from 45.42% to a guided 47-48%.
- Investment-yield optics distorted by the Rs. 700 cr MF holding booking Rs. 12 cr into other income (6.42%
  reported vs 6.67% like-for-like).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** First call under new MD & CEO R. Vijay Anandh. Advances Rs. 67,645 cr (vs Rs. 54,020 cr
  1QFY26, "25% credit growth"); deposits Rs. 79,342 cr (+21%); average CASA Rs. 20,062 cr (+22%, 5th straight
  sequential rise); CD ratio 85%. Interest income Rs. 1,985 cr (+24%); other income Rs. 243 cr (treasury
  Rs. 52 cr vs Rs. 29 cr); **operating profit Rs. 581 cr (+29%, highest ever)**; **PAT Rs. 383 cr (+25%,
  highest ever)**. NIM 3.78%; yield on advances 9.79% (vs ~9.80%); cost of deposits 5.56% (vs 5.60%);
  borrowings interest Rs. 94 cr (vs Rs. 72.50 cr); yield on investments 6.42% (6.67% ex-MF reclass);
  C/I 45.42% (vs 46.15%); ROA 1.57% (vs 1.55%). GNPA 1.73% (vs 2.99%), NNPA Rs. 405 cr / 0.61% (vs 1.20%) —
  12th straight quarter of improvement; PCR 85% with TWO / 65% without (vs 79% / 61%); slippages Rs. 195 cr vs
  recovery Rs. 206 cr; SMA 0/1/2 = 1.20/0.70/0.90 = 2.85% (vs 7.12% Jun-25, 10.78% Sep-24); LCR 150%. Gold
  ~30-31% of book, avg LTV 62.07%; branches 1,000; ECLGS Rs. 800 cr to date; FCNR Rs. 150 cr. One-offs:
  Rs. 700 cr MF investment → Rs. 12 cr into other income; branch roll-out front-loaded, staff hike from July.
  Guidance: credit +2-3% vs industry; mix gold 31-32% / MSME 55-60% / retail ~10% (gold ceiling 33%);
  NIM 3.65-3.70%; cost of deposits 5.60-5.70%; C/I 47-48% FY27 (aspiration <45%); ROA 1.55-1.65% FY,
  exit 1.60-1.65%; credit cost ~0.40%; slippages Rs. 700-750 cr (1.20-1.30%); ECL ~0.45% of book / ≤0.65% of
  CAR; ECLGS pool Rs. 2,000-2,500 cr; DSA 1-2% of book. AGM 14-Aug-2026 at Kumbakonam. CRAR not quantified.
- _next Q → check: NIM vs 3.65-3.70% guide; C/I vs 47-48% once the July staff hike lands; **other income
  Rs. 243 cr → 300-320 cr — the whole 1.65% exit-ROA bridge**; MSME utilisation recovering from 70% toward
  73-74% on the India-EU/Tirupur pickup; advances growth vs "industry +2-3%"; recovery > slippages streak (11th
  quarter); gold share vs 31-32% and LTV vs 62.07% against the gold price; ECLGS Rs. 800 cr → Rs. 2,000-2,500 cr;
  ECL 0.45% assessment at transition; large-industry book vs Rs. 19,000 Mn; whether Dr. N. Kamakodi joins the
  board as Non-Executive Director._
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)

outlook.body:
- **Credit growth:** *"at least two, three percent over and above that of the industry"* — reaffirmed from the
  4QFY26 call; MSME specifically also *"2%, 3% more than the credit system growth."*
- **Loan mix (steady state):** gold **31-32%**, MSME **55-60%**, secured retail **~10%**. Gold comfort ceiling
  **33%** (*"we would be more comfortable with 33"*).
- **NIM:** **3.65%-3.70%** *"in the next few quarters"* (from 3.78%) — driver: *"term deposit rates on the verge
  of rising due to high demand… will impact NIM levels by around 5 bps; once the situation eases, it will come
  back to normal."* Longer-term MD is more upbeat: *"more or less, we should be there with 3.70%, 3.750% range
  on a long term."*
- **Cost of deposits:** **5.60%-5.70%** (from 5.56%); borrowing cost *"of present status of Rs. 94 crores to
  continue for the next two quarters."*
- **Cost-to-income:** **47%-48% for FY27** (from 45.42%) — *"our hikes are from July… we expect the cost to move
  up."* Three-to-four-year aspiration: *"less than 45%."*
- **ROA:** **1.55%-1.65% full-year**, **exit ROA 1.60%-1.65%** (from 1.57%). Predicated on other income moving
  from Rs. 243 cr toward *"300, 320."*
- **Credit cost:** *"at a steady state, we should be around 0.40"*.
- **Slippages:** **Rs. 700-750 cr for the year**, i.e. *"1.20%, 1.30%"*; recovery > slippages expected to
  continue in the current (Q2) quarter.
- **ECL transition:** provisioning requirement assessed at **~0.45% of the loan book**, capital consumption
  *"should not be more than 0.65% on the CAR"*; incremental flow-basis impact *"very, very negligible."*
- **ECLGS:** total expected uptake **Rs. 2,000-2,500 cr** under the scheme (Rs. 800 cr to date).
- **DSA / third-party sourcing:** capped at **1%-2% of the overall bank book**.
- **Ticket size:** deliberately stable; *"we really are not keen to do above Rs. 10 crores."*
> Guidance framing to verify next quarter: this is the first full guidance set owned by the **new MD**, and it
> is *lower* than the delivered quarter on all three of NIM, C/I and (implicitly) fee income — an
> under-promise posture, or a genuine step-down. Q2FY27 is the test.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
- **MSME:** average disbursal **~Rs. 3,500 cr per quarter**, against **Rs. 900 cr of repayment per month**
  (*"every quarter we almost come down by Rs. 2,700 crores"*) — so gross origination is far above the ~15% net
  book growth the analysts pushed back on.
- **Working-capital utilisation dropped 73% → 70%** this quarter, which MD says cost roughly *"another 2%, 3%
  more in MSME"* of growth. He frames the drop as prudence, not weakness: *"if somebody is conscious of what
  they are utilizing, I think it's a good sign."*
- **ECLGS:** Rs. 200 cr last quarter → **Rs. 800 cr as of the call**, against a Rs. 2,000-2,500 cr expected pool.
  MD: *"ECGLS is something which was fabulous, which came at the right time because there were not any stress…
  it's only the working capital cycle for that ECGLS has helped them to come back to normal."*
- **FCNR window:** only **Rs. 150 cr** mobilised so far under the RBI benefit — immaterial.
- **Named demand pockets:** Tirupur textiles (*"very positive on the momentum"* on the India-Europe agreement),
  Sriperumbudur auto/automobile (*"our share can considerably go up there"*), paper & corrugated boxes in
  Kangeyam / Palladam.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline (loan pipeline / growth drivers)

outlook.body:
- **Other income rebuild** is the stated ROA lever: three heads named — **processing fee** (a function of
  disbursement), **suit recovery** (from write-off recoveries) and **insurance income** (*"we always keep it at
  last because we really don't push that much"*) — i.e. insurance distribution is an untapped lever by choice.
- **AI / automation in operations** as the cost-to-income lever: *"we want to maintain the cost to income at the
  desired level with automation with AI in some of the spaces… the operational space we have invested much in
  AI, I think, we should get this cost further coming down."*
- **India-EU trade agreement** as the MSME demand unlock, textiles first: *"people are really gung-ho about the
  future business prospects considering the European agreement which has been signed, particularly in the
  textile space."* MD expects utilisation to recover above threshold on this.
- **Auto cluster (Sriperumbudur)** named as under-penetrated share opportunity.

open.item: Retail contribution to total advances targeted at about 2% to 2.5% for FY26, rising to 8-9% over the next 3-4 years; MSME remains the growth focus.
About INR 1,782 crore of deposits still to be repriced over the next couple of quarters, supporting cost-of-deposits reduction.
IFC-linked solar/renewable energy lending portfolio (~INR 500 crore at Q2) is progressing slowly; expected to complete deployment before end of calendar year 2026.
Effective tax rate (~20%) expected to continue for another 2-4 quarters, possibly to completion of next year, depending on write-offs and incremental provisions.
Operating expenses expected to be elevated 15% to 18% over last year in FY27 due to accelerated branch openings (70 branches opened in the first month).
FY27 credit-deposit ratio endeavour is 85% to 87% based on credit growth, with deposit growth matched to credit growth via CASA and granular term deposits.
Bank launching segment-specific products for women and senior citizens and enhancing savings/current account propositions in FY27.
Having opened its 1,000th branch, bank plans to keep the pace of ~75 new branches per year (50 opened in April, remaining ~25 toward year-end) with a branch-led business model.
Fee income to other income expected in the 55% to 60% range in FY27, same as last year.
NIM expected to stay stable for FY27 within a narrow band of about 5 to 10 basis points around the FY26 level (3.74% full-year; 3.87% Q4).
Bank aims to exit FY27 with at least 10 bps higher ROA, targeting 1.65% to 1.67% (from ~1.56% in FY26), driven by retail income and lower cost-to-income.
FY27 portfolio mix planned as MSME ~55-60%, JL 30-35%, remainder secured retail; third-party sourcing kept to only 1-2% of overall book.
For FY27, bank targets advances growth 2% to 3% above the industry (mid-teen to high-teen), with MSME dominating and gold/secured retail as enhancers.
Management flags US-Iran conflict, oil/inflation risk and a 10-15% gold price fall as watch items, but says built-in gold LTV cushion (per-gram capped ~INR 10,000-10,300) leaves no current concern.
Gold loan share (~30-32% of book) is treated as near the internal upper band; increases limited to ~1-2% either way.
Over the next ~15 years management expects at least a 50% reduction in credit cost (which averaged ~0.60% over the last 15 years, 0.04% in FY26), aided by AI-based underwriting.
With 20%+ Tier-1, management expects the new ECL circular to be adjusted through opening reserves with no P&L impact and likely no future ECL provisioning requirement.
Bank can lend another ~INR 3,000 crore of advances without raising deposits while maintaining LCR, given LCR calculation changes and ~100% incremental CD ratio.
MSME portfolio yield expected to be maintained around 9.5% with only 10-15 bps variation.
Fee income to assets expected to stay stable around 1.2% with only INR 5-10 crore average incremental jump per quarter.

verdicts.item: Management targets restoring credit growth to double-digit and at least industry level for FY25, having already reached 10% YoY advances growth in Q1FY25.
verdicts.note: 'we have achieved growth double-digit over the last eight quarters up to the Q4 financial year '26' including 'the Q1 financial year '25' - FY25 double-digit/industry goal confirmed. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Bank aims to keep credit-deposit ratio around 85%, with deposit growth broadly matching credit growth.
verdicts.note: 'Our average CD ratio for the financial year '26 stood at 85 %'; 'deposit growth matched with that of the credit growth... deposits had grown by 23%.'

verdicts.item: FY25 slippages guided to INR 800 crore or less (INR 555 crore in 9M), reducing to about INR 700 crore in FY26.
verdicts.note: 'slippage for the whole year will be about INR700 to INR750 crores, compared to about INR800 crores plus during the financial year 2025' - both years met the guide.

verdicts.item: Recoveries expected to exceed slippages for the next two quarters (through H1FY26).
verdicts.note: 'the recovery is more than the slippage in the current quarter as well, which is the trend we have been seeing for the last several quarters' - covers and extends past H1FY26.

verdicts.item: NIM guided to around 3.6% plus or minus 10 basis points for FY26, expected to be stable for the year despite rate cuts.
verdicts.note: 'For the year ended 31st March 2026, the net interest margin is 3.74 %, which is 14 basis points more than the 3.60 %... in the financial year 2025' - at/above the FY26 band (beat). [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Cost-to-income ratio guided at 48% to 50% for FY25 as retail expenses take off, expected to decline once retail delivers; Q3FY25 at 46.58%.
verdicts.note: expired: no update 4Q past horizon Q4FY25

verdicts.item: Bank targeting to raise PCR without technical write-off toward ~60% to bring it closer to industry levels (59% in Q3FY25).
verdicts.note: 'PCR without a technical write-off improved to 65 % compared to 60 %' - exceeded the ~60% target.

verdicts.item: Credit cost expected to remain flat around 60-65 basis points, subject to economic cycle and slippages.
verdicts.note: '0.09 in '24-'25 and 0.04 in '25-'26... The average works out to about 0.60' - net credit cost well below the 60-65 bps guide (different basis: net of TW recoveries). [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Branch network to reach about 850 to 875 branches by March 31, 2025, expanding into North and West besides South.
verdicts.note: expired: no update 4Q past horizon Q4FY25

verdicts.item: Yield on advances (9.81% Q3FY25) expected to drop by about 0.10-0.12% toward 9.7% over the year as rate cuts flow through, but full-year margin stays stable.
verdicts.note: 'For financial year '26, the same was 9.75 % against 9.79 % in the financial year '25'; NIM rose to 3.74% - yield eased modestly while full-year margin stayed stable/higher.

verdicts.item: Recovery from written-off pool (INR 1,400 crore book) expected to continue at INR 60-80 crore per quarter run-rate.
verdicts.note: 'INR78 crores from the technically written-off accounts' - within the INR60-80 cr/quarter run-rate.

verdicts.item: Bank guides to mid-teen to high-teen credit growth for FY26, 2-3% over industry; achieved 21% YoY in Q3FY26 and expects to end FY26 in high-teen growth.
verdicts.note: 'we will end up with high teen growth for the financial year 2026, which will be over and above the industry level growth'; actual 26% advance / 24% business - met and exceeded.
